title: Engineering training review
introduction: The purpose of this exercise is to define the model’s priority tasks, reference answers and evaluation criteria. Work through the five sections. For each example, read the source notes, record the required answer, then compare it with the draft reference. Identify corrections, missing evidence and serious errors. Add cases or topics the training should cover, then submit your feedback.
estimated_time: About 10 minutes for a first pass; 20–30 minutes for all examples.

categories.title: Where this would help
categories.intro: Identify and rank specific engineering tasks to determine the initial training scope.

categories.title: Numbers and pressure references
categories.intro: Read the source notes and record the required answer before opening the draft reference. Check the calculation, units, pressure basis and assumptions.

categories.title: Missing facts and judgment
categories.intro: Specify when the model should request information, explain a limitation or withhold a conclusion.

categories.title: Exceptions, sources and Norm
categories.intro: Identify cases, source material and expert contributions that would extend the training beyond the handbook examples.

categories.title: Your recommendation
categories.intro: Specify revisions, acceptance criteria and additional tasks for the next demonstration.

questions.title: What would you want help with first?
questions.question: Think of a recent job. Which check, investigation or document task took more effort than it should have? What happened, and who needed the result?
questions.help: Describe an actual task and remove identifying client details.
questions.why: Select a useful first task before expanding the training corpus.

questions.title: Define a useful result
questions.question: For that task, complete: Given [inputs], help [person] prepare [output] so they can [decision]. What would you still check or decide yourself?
questions.help: Include the information usually missing, and the calculation or evidence you would expect to see.
questions.why: Turn a broad priority into a trainable task and a reviewable output.

questions.title: How would pressure checking rank?
questions.question: Where would checking pressure bases, units and missing assumptions rank against your other priorities? Describe how often errors arise, their consequence and the review effort. Suggest a more valuable starting topic if appropriate.
questions.help: State the priority and basis for the ranking. Mark unknown frequency, effort or consequence explicitly.
questions.why: Prioritize training tasks by practical value.

questions.title: Gauge to absolute
questions.question: A transmitter is explicitly referenced to local atmosphere. It reads 27.4 psig; the relevant atmospheric pressure is 13.2 psia. Convert to psia.
questions.evidence_note: Provided paraphrased evidence notes (not verbatim source): DOE-HDBK-1012-1-92:pdf-035: gauge pressure is relative to the relevant atmospheric reference; absolute pressure is relative to absolute vacuum. Figure 2 illustrates pressure references, not plant piping. DOE-HDBK-1012-1-92:pdf-036: With compatible psi units, equation 1-9 is P_abs = P_atm + P_gauge. For a positive vacuum-depression magnitude, equation 1-10 is P_abs = P_atm - P_vac. The diver/watch example assumes 14.7 psia and gives a mass density in lbm/ft3 with P = rho H. DOE-HDBK-1012-1-92:pdf-037: The worked example again assumes 14.7 psia; the page lists rounded water-column and mercury-column equivalents. These examples do not measure local atmosphere. Author-defined demo scope: do not use the implicit hydrostatic mass/force convention or rounded column conversions as validated recipes. These pressure definitions do not establish equipment operating limits.
questions.help: State the required calculations, assumptions, evidence and follow-up questions.
questions.tolerance: +/-0.05 psi rounding tolerance, not sensor accuracy
requirements: Uses the supplied local atmospheric reference
Reports psia and shows the calculation
questions.source_label: DOE handbook, PDF pages 35–37 (printed HT-01 pages 9–11)

questions.title: Where would the obvious answer fail?
questions.question: Describe a case where a familiar rule or plausible diagnosis misled people. What was known initially, what was missing, and what observation changed the conclusion? Where does the lesson stop applying?
questions.help: Distinguish something you observed from a reconstructed memory or hypothetical example. Identify client records by description only.
questions.why: Find rare but consequential cases; keep initial evidence separate from hindsight.

questions.title: Where could Norm help most?
questions.question: Which two or three problems would you ask Norm about first? What would you ask him to explain that a handbook leaves out? If interested, would his best next contribution be a case, a critique of answers, a teaching discussion, or something else?
questions.help: Name another specialist if the task requires different expertise.
questions.why: Begin with focused expertise before discussing broader archive access.

questions.title: What evidence would improve the examples?
questions.question: Which report, drawing, datasheet, calculation, teaching note or resolved discussion would help? What would it teach, who likely owns it, and what restrictions might apply?
questions.help: Nominate material; do not paste private records or assume that access grants training permission.
questions.why: Build a source shortlist with ownership and scope, separate from rights approval.

questions.title: What would earn your confidence?
questions.question: What should the next demonstration show before you would use an assistant’s draft? Name a useful result, a failure that would stop you using it, and the person who should review it.
questions.help: Suggest one small input package and one observable success criterion.
questions.why: Set task-specific acceptance criteria rather than relying on a general accuracy percentage.

questions.title: What have we missed?
questions.question: Add tasks, exceptions, corrections or questions not covered above. Enter notes or paste a transcript.
questions.help: This draft supports text and pasted transcripts. The separate voice-intake work can supply reviewed transcript passages later.
questions.why: Record additional tasks and exceptions for follow-up.
